text:
ashley: Quick sync — I'm proposing we split the console render pipeline into two interfaces: a compact streaming renderer for small widgets and a bulk tile renderer for heavy panels. Goal: reduce tail latency for dashboards with many tiny cards.

kevin: +1 on intent. Curious where RBAC checks live in this split. pre-render auth or post-render filter? :thinking_face:

maria: My take: do auth as early as possible to avoid leaking any attrs into downstream renderers. Pre-fetch perms at query ingress, attach a perm-hash to the request.

jamie: Perm-hash sounds good. But we need to decide cache keys: tenant+perm-hash+route? otherwise cache poisoning across roles.

ashley: Exactly. Cache key proposal: <tenant_id>:<view_id>:<perm-hash>:<time-bucket>. That keeps compact renderer fast and safe.

kevin: Tradeoff: pre-auth means more calls to auth service for high-frequency small widgets. Could hammer auth. Maybe a light in-process LRU for perm-hash TTL=30s?

maria: LRU + async refresh on miss seems reasonable. We track auth_hitrate and auth_latency. If auth_latency spikes, fallback to bulk renderer.

jamie: Also consider doing permissive render + post-filter for low-sensitivity charts (metrics only) to save auth calls. Ops wants clear classification per widget.

ashley: Good point — add a widget metadata flag: sensitivity: low|high. If low -> post-filter allowed, else pre-auth required. We'll need product to annotate widgets.

kevin: How about interface shapes? I propose two endpoints: /render/compact (streaming, small payload) and /render/tile (batch, accepts list of widget descriptors). Compact returns SSE chunks. Tile returns a single blob.

jamie: Agree. Also add header X-Perm-Hash and X-Render-Mode for observability.

maria: For caching and cache invalidation: compact renderer should leverage shared prefix cache for partial prefixes (like template+static-assets). Tile renderer uses tenant-scoped tile cache with explicit TTL.

ashley: We'll need to tweak router to route by widget size + sensitivity + SLO. Pseudo-rule: if widget.estimated_cost < 50ms && sensitivity != high -> compact; else tile.

kevin: Who owns cost estimation? frontend can annotate estimated_cost, fallback to historical estimator in backend.

ashley: Ownership: eng-platform owns router + runtime. Eng-frontend owns annotations + product changes. We'll add a small shim where backend trains a per-widget EWMA for cost.

tomas: For telemetry, track p50/p95/p99 for both renderers, cache hit rates, auth calls per render, and per-tenant error rate. Need dashboards and alerts if p95_compact > 300ms or auth_error_rate > 1%.

jamie: Also surface a per-view breakdown: fraction of widgets routed to compact vs tile. That helps rollouts.

maria: Rollout plan: feature flag "compact-render-v1". Canary at 5% of tenants -> 25% -> 100% over 2 weeks. Automatic rollback if p95 increases by >20% or error rate rises.

ashley: Add a fallback policy: if compact renderer fails or times out, router retries on /render/tile with a single retry. Timeout for compact = 250ms by default.

kevin: Need a contract for responses so UI isn't fragile. Suggest envelope: { status, chunks: [...], render_mode, cache_hint }. For streaming, send chunks incrementally then final status.

jamie: Include a small example for the frontend to parse:
```
// compact
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
:chunk: {"widget_id":"w1","html":"<svg>...</svg>"}
:chunk: {"widget_id":"w1","meta":{"render_ms":12}}
:done: {"status":"ok"}
```

maria: Nice. Also include a meta path for RBAC errors so UI can show permission-specific empty states instead of generic error. E.g., {"status":"forbidden","reason":"no_view_perm"}.

tomas: Ops: implement a canary job to run synthetic dashboards against both renderers and compare diffs. We'll tag mismatches and false negatives.

ashley: Security note: ensure perm-hash is HMAC'ed with request nonce and not reversible. Also strip any user identifiers before logging.

kevin: Perf thought: compact renderer should avoid cold-view compilation. Precompile widget templates and store compiled bytecode per-view. Warmup strategy: compile-on-deploy + async precompile for top N views.

jamie: Cost modeling: estimate tokens and CPU-time for each renderer. We'll factor this into Dedicated capacity hints. Compact renderer should be cheaper per-request but more SLO-sensitive.

maria: QA checklist: unit tests for routing rules, auth LRU semantics, cache key collisions, and end-to-end test with synthetic perms.

ashley: Action items:
- eng-platform: implement router + endpoints + metrics (kevin, jamie)
- eng-frontend: add widget sensitivity + cost annotation (maria)
- ops/sre: canary harness + alerts (tomas)
- security: perm-hash review (security team)

kevin: I'll sketch an RFC draft with API shapes and rollout plan by EOD tomorrow.

maria: I'll work on permission LRU prototype and share perf numbers.

deploy-bot: canary feature flag "compact-render-v1" created at 1762510200, targeting 5% tenants.

sre-bot: synthetic-run started for canary at 1762510300. Will report diffs to #incidents.

jamie: thanks everyone. Let's sync 30m after kevin's RFC draft to lock contracts.

ashley: Thanks — thread closed for now, will reopen with RFC link.
